classification.difficultyReason: Use the maximum found in earlier parts to split the flight into a rise and a fall, then add the magnitudes of the two height changes.

content.prompt:
A projectile is fired into the air and its height $y$ metres is given by
$$y=9+8t-t^2$$
where $t$ is time in seconds.

children.label: c
children.prompt: When does the particle reach maximum height?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}8-2t&=0\\t&=4\end{align*}$$
The velocity is positive before $t=4$ and negative afterwards, so the height is greatest at $t=4$ s.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Find when the projectile has height $21$ metres.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}9+8t-t^2&=21\\t^2-8t+12&=0\\(t-2)(t-6)&=0\\t&=2\quad\text{or}\quad t=6\end{align*}$$
The height is $21$ m at $2$ s and $6$ s.

children.label: f
children.prompt: Find when the projectile reaches the ground.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}9+8t-t^2&=0\\t^2-8t-9&=0\\(t-9)(t+1)&=0\\t&=9\quad\text{or}\quad t=-1\end{align*}$$
The projectile reaches the ground $9$ s after launch. The negative time is before launch.

children.label: g
children.prompt: Sketch the graph showing the height of the projectile over time $t$.

answer.short: A downward-opening parabola from $(0,9)$ to $(9,0)$ with vertex $(4,25)$.
answer.worked: Plot the initial point $(0,9)$, the maximum $(4,25)$ and the landing point $(9,0)$. Draw the downward-opening parabola between launch and landing, with $t$ on the horizontal axis and $y$ on the vertical axis.

spec.sourceRegion: Answer book printed page 356, Exercise 7L Q6(g)
spec.description: Arrowed time and height axes, integer time ticks from 1 to 9, height ticks every 3 m from 3 to 27, square major grid and blue height curve.
spec.mathematics: y=9+8t-t^2 on 0≤t≤9, with endpoints (0,9) and (9,0) and vertex (4,25). Grid steps are 1 on the t-axis and 3 on the y-axis.

children.label: h
children.prompt: How far will the projectile travel in the first $9$ seconds?

answer.short: $41$ m. Add the rise from $9$ m to $25$ m and the fall from $25$ m to ground level.
answer.worked:
The projectile rises from $9$ m to $25$ m, then falls to ground level.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total distance}&=\bigl[(25-9)+(25-0)\bigr]\,\text{m}\\\text{Total distance}&=(16+25)\,\text{m}\\\text{Total distance}&=41\,\text{m}\end{align*}$$
